published_statement: HPS p.4: 'Carrying out these straightforward but rather lengthy steps we find that the semiclassical Einstein equations for a conformally coupled scalar (xi = 1/6) are as follows (K^2 = 1/(5760 pi)):' followed by eqs. (5)-(7), each of the form G^mu_nu (left side) = K^2 [ ... + ln f ( ... ) ]. With eq. (3), G^nu_mu = 8 pi <T^nu_mu>, this makes <T^nu_mu> = (K^2/(8 pi)) [ ... ] = (1/(46080 pi^2)) [ ... ]. Footnote [19]: 'We use units such that hbar = c = G = 1'. Footnote [20]: 'We have also set the scalar mass and temperature to zero: m = kappa = 0. In this case, the arbitrary renormalization scale parameter mu appearing in (T^nu_mu)_log can be absorbed into the definition of f.' HPS use K in print twice more: eq. (8) contains K^-2 r(0)^2, and eq. (9) sets r(0) = sqrt(-16 K^2 ln f(0)); p.7 prints 'r(0) ~ 67 l_P' for f(0) = f''(0) = 1, r''(0) = 0, and 'r(0) ~ 0.02 l_P' for ln f(0) = -2/3.
published_hypotheses: A (single) conformally coupled scalar field, xi = 1/6 (p.3 'conformally coupled scalar field'; p.4 'for a conformally coupled scalar (xi = 1/6)').
Scalar mass and temperature zero, m = kappa = 0 (footnote [20]).
Units hbar = c = G = 1, MTW sign conventions (footnote [19]); G^nu_mu = 8 pi <T^nu_mu> (eq. (3)).

<T^nu_mu> taken in the Anderson-Hiscock-Samuel analytic approximation, PRD 51 4337 (eq. (4), ref. [18]), rewritten in f(l), r(l) (p.4) -- a hypothesis of the bracket, not of the scalar normalisation K^2.
Static spherically symmetric metric in proper-distance gauge, eq. (2).

rederivation.outcome: ALL PASS, exit 0 (~10 s). C1: 8 pi/(46080 pi^2) - 1/(5760 pi) simplifies to 0; 46080 = 8 x 5760. C2: K = 0.00743385048396988 l_P; the tree's withdrawn typed 0.0074335 differs by 3.5e-7, i.e. in the 5th significant digit, confirming the WITHDRAWN entry at hpscentre.py:335-336. C3: HPS eq. (8) at f(0) = f''(0) = 1, r''(0) = 0 reduces to -4 r^4 + K^-2 r^2 = 0, root r(0) = 1/(2K) = 12 sqrt(10 pi) = 67.2599 l_P against HPS's printed 'r(0) ~ 67 l_P'. C4: eq. (9) at ln f(0) = -2/3 gives r(0) = sqrt(15)/(90 sqrt(pi)) = 0.024279 l_P against printed 'r(0) ~ 0.02 l_P'. Controls: K^2 = 1/(2880 pi), 1/(46080 pi^2), 1/(720 pi) give 47.6, 337, 23.8 l_P for C3 -- only 1/(5760 pi) reproduces the printed 67. C5 (the independent normalisation): the NON-LOG brackets of eqs. (5)-(7), transcribed afresh from the text layer (not imported from the tree), traced as tt + ll + 2 thth, and fitted over arbitrary f(l), r(l) against a Riem^2 + b Ric^2 + c R^2 + d box R with the curvature computed from eq. (2) (MTW convention): unique solution a = 16, b = -16, c = 0, d = 16. So 8 pi <T> = K^2 x 16 (Riem^2 - Ric^2 + box R), which is exactly the conformal-scalar anomaly (1/(2880 pi^2))(Riem^2 - Ric^2 + box R) iff K^2 = 1/(5760 pi), with positive sign. The Riem^2 coefficient alone (scheme-independent; box R is shiftable by a local R^2 counterterm) already fixes K^2. The log part was not used; its tracelessness hinges on the M1 reading the tree records separately and is not this key.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for K^2: nothing measured enters this result, so there is no datum the authors could have lacked. K^2 = 1/(5760 pi) is the one-loop normalisation of a free massless conformal scalar in Planck units; C5 shows it is exactly what the (state-independent, scheme-independent in its Riem^2 part) conformal anomaly 1/(2880 pi^2) requires of HPS's printed brackets, and C3/C4 show HPS's own printed numbers (67 l_P, 0.02 l_P) were computed with it. Evidence against M's hypothesis here: an internal-consistency triangle (printed K^2, printed eqs. (5)-(7) trace, printed eq. (8)/(9) numbers) closes exactly. Where later knowledge WOULD matter is applicability, not accuracy: HPS's model has one massless conformally coupled scalar; the measured world's fields (a massive Higgs doublet with no measured xi = 1/6, fermions, gauge bosons) are not that model, and K^2 grows with the number of fields, so K is the scale of HPS's model and not a measured physical scale. That is a named hypothesis (N = 1, m = kappa = 0, xi = 1/6), not an error, and the tree only uses K inside HPS's model. The only measured constant anywhere near it, l_P, is unchanged CODATA 2018 -> 2022 and is not used by the tree.

what_would_change_the_grade: NARROWED if a tree site applies K (or a K-scaled length such as FIRST_NEGATIVE_M_THROAT_LP) to a field content other than one massless conformal scalar (N != 1, m != 0, T != 0, xi != 1/6) without rescaling. A discrepancy (not WRONG) would be recorded if the journal PRL text or Popov's (B1)-(B3) printed a prefactor other than 1/(5760 pi) resp. 1/(46080 pi^2); C3-C5 would then decide which printing is consistent. WRONG would need the conformal-scalar anomaly coefficient to differ from 1/(2880 pi^2), which would contradict the heat-kernel a2 coefficient.
